data.remark:
Exact (a*b) mod p from two trained ReLU cells on a carry-save pipeline — 45 s for the full 1100-case run, T10 at 100%.

Two learned cells (full-adder, full-subtractor; 8-row Boolean functions) are the only value-transforming components. The accumulator is held in redundant carry-save form, so adding a vector is a single elementwise, depth-1 layer of full-adder cells (3:2 compression) with no carry propagation; doubling is a shift; register overflow is compensated by injecting 2^Wd mod p, itself computed in-network from p by the subtractor cell; carries are resolved exactly once per phase. A fixed Horner recurrence over the raw operand bits composes these steps. No prefix scan, and no value-driven control flow anywhere: all wrap bookkeeping uses fixed, unconditional round counts with masked (possibly zero) binary addends. Batches are internally sub-grouped by prime bit-length.

Official playground, two revisions: frontier tier T10, overall_accuracy 100% (1000/1000 on tiers 1-10), 45.0 s and 46.5 s wall-clock, identical per-tier counts; Tier-0 diagnostic 80/100. A full local evaluation with the official open-source runner reproduces it end to end (overall_accuracy 1.0, highest_tier_above_90 = 10, deterministic: true per the runner's own check).

Why it is exact rather than accurate: inter-cell thresholding keeps every cell input binary, so each cell's complete input space is its truth table. Exactness is certified by exhaustive verification and preserved under composition — at any operand width and for any operand family, including the power-of-two-adjacent operands that are a known residual for statistically trained rollouts. Cells are margin-hardened (min |logit| >= 6.07) and run under bf16 autocast with fp32 thresholding, verified exhaustively at 0 decision flips. Randomizing the trained weights collapses accuracy to 0%.

Two findings that may be useful to others working this lane: (1) the determinism check builds a single batch mixing all tiers, so any per-batch setup cost that scales with the spread of prime bit-lengths explodes there while every per-tier run stays fast — sub-grouping by bit-length fixes it; (2) CUDA graphs are not the lever for this workload shape, but flattening per-step depth is.
